title: How the Nampa Club America attendance dispute narrowed
summary: Tracks Owens’s allegation of compulsory assembly attendance, Kolvet’s opt-out counteraccount, and the ensuing distinction between opting out of an assembly and opting into a chapter. It does not independently establish confinement, donor deception or school policy.

milestones.label: Compulsion alleged
milestones.proposition: Owens accuses promoters of presenting a school assembly as voluntary club growth while omitting that students were expected to attend and parents could not attend.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 1151–1391 seconds, including redacted parent/student reports and the 500-plus promotion. This is her initial accusation, not independent proof of confinement or donor deception. The subsequent opt-out concession materially qualifies her initial “could not opt out” wording.
milestones.statement_text: Owens accused the event’s promoters of dishonestly presenting a school assembly as voluntary club growth while omitting that students were expected to attend and parents were barred.
milestones.speaker: Candace Owens

evidence.text: Owens accused the event’s promoters of dishonestly presenting a school assembly as voluntary club growth while omitting that students were expected to attend and parents were barred.
evidence.speaker: Candace Owens
excerpts: And yet, remarkably, after I break the story, they then share this, which is just to me, it's fundamentally dishonest. It's like a lie by severe omission. ... When you're sharing an audience attendance like, wow, look at all these kids who showed up to hear Erika (Erika Kirk) speak and leaving out the part that they were kind of forced to be there because it's a school assembly. ... I said the students were forced to attend this event as a school assembly. They could not opt out. The parents were informed that they were not allowed to attend alongside them. ... That is true. The parents were told that. It is insane to me that you have administrations forcing events on underage kids and that are trying to spin it to the public as successful club growth. ... It's a fundamentally dishonest presentation. Do we all agree that that's a fundamentally dishonest presentation to tweet that?
